newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling weakens against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling weakens against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling fell against the dollar on Wednesday on increased importer demand, commercial dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 55.74 against the dollar from 55.68 on Tuesday. Against the pound, the shilling was posted at 91.86 from 91.76.
Dealers said the shilling weakened against the dollar on huge orders from the oil industry into the market from Monday.

"The increased demand from the oil companies has come in big orders as they try to cover for their end-year commitments," a commercial dealer said. "What is actually happening is that they are buying in small lots."
Dealers said they expected shilling weakness to continue to the end of the week. "Demand has at last come. From Tuesday we saw a turnaround in the direction of the shilling," one said.
The money market was still liquid with rates stuck at 10-15 levels from 10-13 percent on Tuesday.
